groups.title: Node.js runtime and Express middleware model
groups.question: Your Express API for the task app freezes for every user while one request generates a large report, and a middleware is not reaching its error handler. Explain how Node and Express process requests.

followUps.Node's non-blocking I/O and why CPU-boun: Why does one CPU-heavy request slow down every other user?
followUps.Express middleware execution order and e: How does an error in middleware reach the error handler?

evidence.text: Node handles I/O like database calls without blocking the event loop.
CPU-heavy code runs on the single main thread and blocks every other request.
Heavy work should be moved to worker threads, a queue or another service.
Middleware runs in the order it is registered.
next passes control to the next middleware.
next with an error skips normal middleware and goes to error-handling middleware.

notEnough: Only saying middleware runs in order.

groups.title: REST API conventions for a MEAN backend
groups.question: Your Angular app on port 4200 calls an Express API on port 3000 to manage tasks. Explain how you would design the API's URLs and methods and make the browser allow the calls.

followUps.Resource-based URL design and correct HT: How would you design URLs and methods for tasks?
followUps.CORS configuration for Angular consuming: Why does the browser block the Angular app's calls, and how do you configure CORS?

evidence.text: URLs name resources like /tasks/42, not actions.
GET reads, POST creates, PATCH updates part of a task and DELETE removes it.
Consistent conventions make the API predictable for the Angular client.
Different ports count as different origins, so the browser applies CORS rules.
The server must allow the Angular app's origin.
In production, only the deployed frontend's origin should be allowed.

groups.title: Structuring and running a MEAN Express API
groups.question: Your Express app has all logic in route handlers, and it crashes hours after deploying because an environment variable was missing. Explain how you would structure the code and configuration.

followUps.Router modules, controllers, and the ser: What do routers, controllers and services each do?
followUps.Environment config with dotenv and start: Why validate environment variables at startup?

evidence.text: Routers map URLs to controller functions.
Controllers handle the request and response.
Services hold business logic, so it can be tested and reused independently.

notEnough: Only saying you split code into files.

evidence.text: dotenv loads variables from a .env file into the process environment.
Checking required variables at startup makes the app fail immediately with a clear error.
Otherwise a missing value causes a confusing crash later when it is first used.

groups.title: Input validation and error handling
groups.question: Users can create tasks with empty titles, and every route has its own try/catch with different error formats. Explain how you would validate input and handle errors consistently.

followUps.express-validator for route-level reques: How would you validate a task's title on the route?
followUps.Centralized error middleware and async e: How do you handle errors from async routes in one place?

evidence.text: Validation rules are chained per field, such as not empty and trimmed.
The handler checks the validation result first.
It returns a 422 with the list of errors if any rule fails.

notEnough: Only saying you validate the body.

evidence.text: A single error middleware with four arguments is registered after all routes.
An async wrapper forwards rejected promises to next with the error.
All errors then get the same response format.

notEnough: Only saying you add error handling.
